messages:
Rina (Vendor Ops): ArcticCompute AG (CH) sent invoice #CH-778 for model evaluation. They charged 7.7% Swiss VAT and asked Redwood to "confirm export status" so they can zero-rate future invoices. They also asked if Redwood will withhold any US taxes. Invoice attached.

Claire (AP): Invoice shows VAT number CHE-123.456.789 MWST and bill-to Redwood Inference LLC (US). We need a clear VAT line, vendor VAT reg (they gave), and if they claim zero-rate then documentation.

Paul (Tax): For Swiss VAT: exports of services to non-residents can be zero-rated if the supplier documents that supply is consumed outside Switzerland. The vendor usually decides but needs proof. Ask for: 1) confirmation they consider the supply an export with legal basis, 2) copy/screenshot of their Swiss VAT registration, and 3) a statement identifying the recipient as a non-Swiss customer and where services are consumed.

Paul (Tax): For US withholding: payments to foreign vendors for services performed entirely outside the US are typically not US-source so no US withholding. But we need a W-8BEN-E on file to evidence foreign status and avoid any backup withholding set by our systems.

Rina (Vendor Ops): Drafting reply to vendor, please edit: ```
Hi ArcticCompute team,

Thanks for the invoice. A few items needed to process payment:
1) Please confirm in writing whether you consider this supply an export of services (supply consumed outside Switzerland) and the legal basis for zero-rating Swiss VAT.
2) Please attach a copy/screenshot of your Swiss VAT registration (UID/CHE number) that matches the VAT number on the invoice.
3) If you intend to zero-rate future invoices, reissue the invoice showing "Export of services - VAT 0%" or provide a corrected invoice.
4) To confirm tax status for US payments please complete and upload Form W-8BEN-E (PDF). This will confirm you are a foreign entity and prevent our system from applying any US withholding.

If you cannot provide the VAT evidence we may process the current invoice as charged which could delay payment while tax reviews the treatment.

Best,
Rina (Vendor Ops)
```

Claire (AP): Add: 'Please include the exact legal name as registered with Swiss UID so our bank name matches.'

Sam (Payments): Also ask them to upload bank details and indicate currency preference (CHF or USD). If we need to gross-up or withhold we will need bank instructions for the net/gross amounts.

Rina (Vendor Ops): Sent. ArcticCompute replied: "We're Swiss-registered and normally zero-rate exports but our billing system applied VAT by mistake. We'll reissue zero-rated invoice and upload W-8BEN-E and Swiss VAT screenshot. Can you confirm you want CHF or USD payment?"

Paul (Tax): Good. Once they reissue as VAT 0% and provide W-8BEN-E we're clear. If they persist in charging Swiss VAT we accept charge for this invoice to avoid hold-ups but log it for reclaim possibility; Swiss reclaim is admin-heavy.

Claire (AP): I'll hold payment until corrected invoice or one business day after we receive W-8BEN-E and VAT screenshot. If they upload both today I'll process.

Sam (Payments): Noted. If they request USD payment, Treasury will apply FX; otherwise pay in CHF. Upload bank details to vendor record.

ArcticCompute AG: Vendor: Thanks, uploading corrected docs now. We'll re-issue invoice CH-778-R1 with VAT 0% and attach W-8BEN-E.

Rina (Vendor Ops): Great. Action: update vendor onboarding checklist to require W-8/W-9 or W-8BEN-E and VAT status for cross-border suppliers to avoid runtime invoices like this. Closing after docs attached. :white_check_mark:
